dse_runs.notes: Spec named infeasible: throughput >= 400 MSPS single-lane with max_abs_err <= 2^-12 (12 bits). Likely needs pipelined/pipelined_m families (fully pipelined, one sample/cycle) rather than iterative. Prioritise pipelined and pipelined_m families; check whether the constraint set is actually satisfiable at all and report the best feasible front plus the closest-to-feasible designs if not.

final_text: The campaign queue held a single spec, `infeasible_dds_400msps` (wideband DDS: `throughput_msps >= 400` single-lane with `max_abs_err <= 2^-12`, minimise LUTs, select min LUTs). I spent the full 400-evaluation L1 budget: the structured DSE graph's first round (100 evals) returned `status infeasible` with the inner architect declaring the spec infeasible, and I then used the remaining 300 evals on three direct NSGA-II family probes — `pipelined` (100), `pipelined_m` (100) and `unrolled_k` (100) — each of which also returned 0 feasible designs. No feasible design ever existed, so the rest of the ladder had nothing to operate on: `simulate_system` reported "nothing feasible to simulate yet", `verify_rtl` and `synthesize` reported no selected design, and `back_annotate` was skipped (no winner change to flag, so no `reexplore` was warranted). I finalized the spec with no winner and a note recording the infeasibility and the budget accounting. The conclusion is that the constraint pair (400 MSPS single-lane throughput together with 12-bit accuracy) is not satisfiable anywhere in the design registry — the spec is correctly named infeasible, and the honest result is an empty front rather than a fabricated selection. All numbers above are tool-reported (LUTs/FFs/Fmax/throughput as cost-model estimates, errors exact from the golden model); no value was estimated or invented by me.
